8.6.9. iLock_Geography.geo_algorithms.pathgen.PathGenerator¶

class iLock_Geography.geo_algorithms.pathgen.PathGenerator(railyard, noPrefix=False, noSuffix=False, branch=True, posOrient=None)¶

Return an object that is used to generate 3-tuple (startNodeIndex, edgeSequence, endNodeIndex), referred to as X{path-tuple} for each valid path of a railyard.

The path-tuple of a path (startNodeIndex, edgeSequence, endNodeIndex) specifies the start node index (of the first edge), the sequence of edges and the end node index (of the last edge) of the path.

Attributes:
  • railyard: The railyard where the path-tuples are generated.
  • graph: The graph of railyard.
  • startNodeIndex: The start node index of a path-tuple, i.e. the start nodex index that connects to the first edge of edgeSequence.
  • edgeSequence: The edges inside of a path.
  • endNodeIndex: The end node index of a path-tuple, i.e. the end node index of the last edge of edgeSequence.
  • visited: The set of nodes visited when generating a path-tuple.

Methods

__init__(railyard[, noPrefix, noSuffix, …]) Constructor.
generate() Iterator over the path-tuples of valid paths in railyard.
getPath() Return a path-tuple.
initPath() Initialize attributes startNodeIndex, endNodeIndex, edgeSequence and visited.
isBentLeg(processedNodeIndex) An utility function that determines if processedNodeIndex connects to a bent leg of a switch.
isEdge(processedNodeIndex, newNodeIndex) A callback function that determines if the edge from processedNodeIndex to newNodeIndex is a valid edge.
isEndNodeIndex() A callback function that determines if endNodeIndex is the end node index for a valid path.
isStartNodeIndex(startNodeIndex) A callback function that determines if startNodeIndex is the start node index for a valid path.
popPath() Pop the last edge from edgeSequence.
pushPath(endNodeIndex) Push the edge ending with endNodeIndex in edgeSequence if it is a valid edge (isEdge returns True).
